page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU resources are allocated on a shared basis, with 16 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 6.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the bottom 10%, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all registering in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with PassMark memory and database operations, consistently perform within average parameters.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation model and AMD EPYC architecture offer a balanced resource density for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. The 1:6 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a cost-effective footprint for memory-leaning applications. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, Redis caching, and moderate database operations, while it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or heavy LLM text generation.
